full_judgment:
Mr. A.K. Badrul Huq, J : The Petitioner, Former Managing Director, Bangladesh Krishi Bank in invoking this Courts inherent jurisdiction under Section 561A of The Code of Criminal Procedure approached this Court on presentation of a Petition for quashing the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 371 of 2000 T.R. No. 68 of 2000 under Section 500 of The Penal Code whereupon Rule was issued calling upon the Complainant-Opposite Party to show cause as to why the proceeding of C.R. Case No. 371 of 2000 laid against accused-petitioner pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka should • not be quashed. 

 5. Learned Magistrate examined the Complainant on oath and recorded an order of Judicial Inquiry and on the basis of Judicial Inquiry the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate had been pleased to take cognizance against the accused-petitioner. The accused-petitioner surrendered before the Court and obtained bail. The petitioner, thereafter, moved this petition for quashing the proceeding of C.R. Case. 

 6. Basic grounds pressed into service for quashing the proceeding of C.R. Case are as follows: i. The allegations made against petitioner contained in the Petition of Complaint filed by Complainant-opposite party having not constituted any offence, the proceeding is liable to be quashed to prevent the abuse of the process of the Court. ii. Regard being had to the fact that the statement in the Rejoinder published in Daily Janakantha dated 26.1.1998 in respect of which the Petition of Complaint was filed having not amounted to imputation on the character of the Complainant and the same having not been at all defamatory, the impugned proceeding against accused-petitioner is nullity in the eye of law and requires to be quashed for ends of Justice. iii. The alleged defamatory statements referred to in the Petition of Complaint do not attribute to petitioner and the impugned proceeding against the petitioner got no legal or factual basis whatsoever and the proceeding is liable to be quashed. iv. The impugned proceeding has caused a unnecessary harassment to the petitioner in discharging his official duty as Chief Executive of the Second Biggest National Bank and the same is a sheer abuse of the process of the Court and liable to be quashed. v. The impugned proceeding is malafide, frivolous, vexatious and the proceeding cannot be continued against the petitioner and the same is liable to be quashed. 

 8. The only point that survives for determination in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case is whether the proceeding launched against accused-petitioner by Complainant opposite party is liable to be quashed or not. 

 10. The inherent power under Section 561A of the Code can be exercised by the High Court Division. (a) To give effect to any order passed under the Code, Or (b) To prevent the abuse of the process of the Court Or (c) Otherwise to secure the ends of Justice. In the backdrop of the provision of law contained under Section 561A of The Code and also of the principles of law enunciated by Superior courts in a series of decisions relating to the exercise of inherent power under Section 561A of The Code the following categories of cases may be given by way of illustration wherein such power can be exercised either to prevent the abuse of process of any court or otherwise to secure ends of Justice, though it is not possible to lay down any precise clearly defined and sufficiently characterised and inflexible guidelines or rigid formulate and to give an exhaustive list of myriad kinds of cases wherein such power should be exercised. i. Where the allegation made in the petition of Complaint or the First Information Report, even if taken their face value and accepted in their entirety, do not prima facie constitute any offence or make out a case against accused. ii. Where the uncontroverted allegations made in the Petition of Complaint or the First Information Report and the evidences collected in support of the same do not dis-close any commission of offence and make out a case against the accused. iii. Where the allegations made in the First Information Report or Complaint are so absurd and inherently improbable on the basis of ' which no prudent person can ever reach a just conclusion that there is sufficient ground for proceeding against the accused. iv. Where a criminal proceeding is manifestly attended with malafide and/or where the proceeding is maliciously instituted with an ulterior motive for wreaking vengeance on the accused and with a view to spite him due to personal grudge. v. Where there is an express legal bar engrafted in any of the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure or the Concerned Act under which a Criminal proceeding is instituted to the institution and continuation of the proceeding and/or where there is specific provision in the Code of Criminal Procedure providing efficacious redress for the grievance of the aggrieved party. ' 

 11. It is always to be remembered that the power of quashing a criminal proceeding should be exercised very sparingly and that is in the rarest of rare case. The Court will not be justified in embarking upon an enquiry as to the legality or genuineness or otherwise of the allegation made in the First Information Report or the Petition of Complaint and that the inherent powers do not confer an arbitrary jurisdiction on the Court to act according to its whim and caprices. The inherent power should not be exercised to stifle a legitimate prosecution though the powers possessed by High Court Division are very wide and the very plentitude of the power requires great caution in its exercise. 

 12. Viewed from the above the question posed now may be answered. 13. The petitioner stands indicted for defamation under Section 499 of Penal Code and punishable under Section 500 of The Penal Code. Section 499 enshrines that whoever by words either spoken or intended to be read or by signs or visible representations, makes or publishes any imputation concerning any person intending to harm, or, knowing or having reason to believe that such imputation will harm the reputation of such person is said except in the cases hereinafter excepted to defame that person. In Section 499 there are Four (4) Explanations, Explanation 1,2,3 and 4 and there are Ten (10) Exceptions. First Exception is imputation of truth which public good requires to be made or published. Second Exception states public conduct of public servants. Third Exception deals with conduct of any per-son touching any public question. Fourth Exception is publication of Reports of proceedings of Court. Fifth Exception is merit of case decided in court or conduct of wit-nesses or others concerned. Sixth Exception is of merit of public performance. Seventh Exception is censure passed in good faith by person having lawful authority over another. Eight Exception is accusation preferred in good faith to authorised person. Ninth Exception concerns with imputation made in good faith by person for protection of his or others interest and Tenth Exception is caution intended for good of person to whom conveyed or for public good. The Ninth exception is material for resolution of the legal controversy debate involved in the quashing matter. 

 18. In view of discussion made above we are of this considered view that the proceeding in C.R. Case No. 371 of 2000 T.R. No. 68 of 2900 pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka is a sheer abuse of the process of the Court and to secure the ends of justice, the proceedings cannot be allowed to be prolonged further and the same is to be quashed. 

 19. Resultantly the Rule is made absolute. The proceeding in CA3. Case No. 371 of 2000 under Section 501) T.R. No. 68 of 2000 of The Penal Code pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka stands quashed.
